I farm the way I have learned over many years: I keep the main land in the wheat-maize rotation, and I leave a smaller part for cotton. I am 72, my family labor is only two people, and I have 12 mu with well irrigation, so I will not make the plan too aggressive. I will put 8 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize, because that is the most familiar and steady system for my land and water conditions. I will keep 4 mu in cotton, because cotton still gives me another source of income, but I do not want too much of it since it takes more field management and more pesticide work. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid types where I think they help me keep yield stable. For fertilizer, I will stay in a moderate range: enough to protect yield, but not so much that I waste money or push weak growth. Since I have well irrigation, I will water wheat more carefully because wheat in my area depends on timely irrigation, while maize and cotton will get fewer irrigations. I will use rotary tillage for wheat and cotton because it is easier for me to manage, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat to save labor and catch the sowing window quickly. My whole plan is to keep work manageable, control costs, and rely on the crops and methods I trust most.
